name: Village Enterprise (Founders Pledge, 2018)
summary: Small business grants, training and mentoring for groups of three entrepreneurs living in extreme poverty in Uganda and Kenya. A re-implementation of Founders Pledge's 2018 cost-effectiveness analysis, based on the 2017 randomised trial in Uganda.

source.title: Women's Empowerment cause report (2018): Village Enterprise cost-effectiveness analysis

sections.title: Our steps: per dollar, and staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' steps after Founders Pledge's bottom line: the cost per outcome turned into outcomes per dollar, then credit by share of resources (staff's forgone pay), which is off by default and in Founders Pledge's view.

source.title: Founders Pledge, Women's Empowerment cost-effectiveness analyses (2018)

rows.explainer: Three years of Uganda's real GDP growth multiplied together (5.106%, 5.188%, 4.657%), from World Bank data read in September 2018. It is growth of the whole economy, not per person (Uganda's population grew about 3% a year), so it overstates the control group's consumption growth a little; we keep Founders Pledge's number.

rows.explainer: The yearly gain over the whole duration, discounted, with the first year undiscounted (the sheet's =PV(rate, years − 1, −gain) + gain). The sheet labels it per household; it is per person, as the cost below is.

Cost per one-year unit of increase in ln(consumption) for one person (USD)
Cost to double consumption for one person for one year (USD)
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's bottom line: $250 to double one person's consumption for a year ($157–367 across its conservative and optimistic durations).

rows.label: Doubled-income years per dollar
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's cost to double one person's consumption for a year, turned around. One doubled-income year is one unit of value, the site's common unit, so nothing else converts.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: The midpoint of our defaults for programs that hand out goods (15%) and those where staff deliver the help (50%), rounded: a large part of the cost of a graduation or business-grant program is the asset or cash grant itself, the rest mostly staff time for training and mentoring. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Field staff and mentors at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Doubled-income years per donor dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
